plan.name: Retry briefly unavailable agent providers
plan.summary: Every Codex and Claude Code run used for drafting statements, planning, building or reviewing retries a terminal provider capacity, rate-limit, overload or dropped-connection error in the same workspace with the same job and agent, for at most four attempts with waits of one, two and four minutes; a configurable wait function lets tests run quickly while checking that real schedule. Each wait releases both Codex turn locks, stops at once on cancellation, and counts against one deadline that starts at the first attempt's turn and also covers reacquiring the turn; ordinary errors, including MCP startup and handshake failures even when their full diagnostic mentions a closed connection, successful runs and the existing thinking-loop fallback keep their present behavior. Provider attempts share the run's original gate, check and test call allowance, Claude Code cost and turn limits and Codex step limit, with tool calls counted before work in state the agent cannot change that survives MCP restarts even without a completed log or agent event, and Codex explicitly forwards this allowance through its MCP server configuration despite its filtered server environment; retries receive only remaining limits, never start after exhaustion, and usage sums all attempts' cost, turns and tool counts while keeping the last attempt's outcome and summary, and a paid Claude attempt disconnected before its final cost conservatively reserves its remaining dollar allowance, retains observed turns and tools, reports the cost as an incomplete estimate and stops without retrying, while a closing result supplies the authoritative cost without double counting. Provider exhaustion fails the step despite usable leftover files or passing checks, and an exhausted build agent or review publishes no pull request; its saved failure survives a watcher restart, retains provider unavailability and the last error, and says that a writer's retry builds the same ratified work again, including its review, through the existing no-PR retry path. Update SPEC.md and README.md with the schedule, released turns, single deadline, shared limits, explicit MCP allowance forwarding, conservative incomplete-cost accounting, cumulative usage, MCP startup failure exclusion and no-PR rebuild behavior, citing D-0026, D-0069, D-0074, D-0108, D-0125, D-0138, D-0154 and D-0122 in the affected SPEC bullets; the merger must record the new provider-retry decision, including its refinement of D-0154's timeout rule, because a plumbing build cannot write decisions/.

tests.name: TestCodexRetriesCapacityWithTheSameJob
tests.says: A Codex build that stops at capacity observes its configured wait and succeeds on its next attempt, keeping its workspace, prompt, permissions, tools, model, effort and transcript without taking a thinking-loop fallback.

tests.name: TestCodexRetriesRateLimitsAndDroppedConnections
tests.says: Codex retries terminal rate limits, dropped connections, an error event without a result, and provider errors reported on stderr.

tests.name: TestClaudeRetriesOverloadAndRateLimits
tests.says: Claude Code retries overloaded and rate-limit errors from result and assistant error events, and a dropped provider connection reported on stderr.

tests.name: TestProviderRetriesAreBoundedAndKeepTheLastError
tests.says: Each provider stops after four unsuccessful attempts with three waits, shortened in the test, saying it was unavailable and preserving the last provider error.

tests.name: TestProviderRetriesUseTheMinuteSchedule
tests.says: Both providers request exactly one-, two- and four-minute waits between four attempts, can recover on the fourth attempt, and never wait or try again after it; an injected wait function observes the real schedule without sleeping for seven minutes.

tests.name: TestProviderRetriesStopAtOrdinaryFailures
tests.says: A temporary provider failure is retried, but ordinary failures, including complete MCP startup diagnostics, stop immediately even after a provider retry, retain the ordinary error and do not report provider unavailability; successful output and tool failures that mention provider errors cause no retry.

tests.name: TestProviderWaitCountsAgainstTheRunTimeout
tests.says: Both providers stop when the original job deadline expires during backoff, retaining the provider error and deadline cause without launching another attempt.

tests.name: TestProviderRetriesKeepTheOriginalDeadline
tests.says: A second failed attempt does not renew the job's time limit; its last error survives expiration during the second wait.

tests.name: TestCodexReleasesBothTurnsDuringProviderWait
tests.says: While a Codex run waits to retry, another step using the same sign-in takes the process turn and the home file lock and finishes before the waiting run resumes.

tests.name: TestCancellingAProviderWaitStopsRetries
tests.says: Cancellation interrupts a pending provider wait promptly and prevents another attempt.

tests.name: TestCodexRetryTurnWaitKeepsTheDeadline
tests.says: Time spent reacquiring the Codex turn after backoff counts against the original deadline, and its expiry leaves the other step running.

tests.name: TestProviderFailureIsPostedAfterSavingTheBuild
tests.says: A failure post made from a saved modeled build retains provider unavailability, the last error and the instruction to retry by building again, even when a final gate report exists, and publishes no pull request.

tests.name: TestProviderExhaustionCannotPublishAPassingBuild
tests.says: Provider exhaustion in a modeled build's agent or review leaves the build failed and needing a person, with no pull request or merge even when its leftover code passes the final gate.

tests.name: TestEveryDraftReportsProviderExhaustionDespiteLeftoverFiles
tests.says: Statement drafts, plumbing plans and plans of issues report provider exhaustion instead of proposing files left by an interrupted attempt.

tests.name: TestPlumbingBuildFailsWhenItsProviderNeverFinishes
tests.says: A plumbing build whose provider never finishes fails with the provider error even if its leftover files pass the checks, and it neither reviews nor takes a thinking-loop fallback.

tests.name: TestPlumbingReviewsRetryAndReportProviderExhaustion
tests.says: The separate review run retries a temporary provider failure and can approve after recovery; when its time budget expires instead, it does not approve and retains the provider diagnostic.

tests.name: TestProviderExhaustionRetryRebuildsAndReviewsTheRatifiedPlan
tests.says: An exhausted build agent or review publishes no pull request; after saving and restarting, the failure preserves its last provider error and says retry builds again, and a writer's retry rebuilds the ratified plan, completes a fresh review of that code and merges only after CI passes.

tests.name: TestProviderRetriesSumUsageAndKeepTheLastOutcome
tests.says: Both providers sum every attempt's cost, turns and tool counts while preserving the last outcome and summary across recovery, ordinary failure and exhaustion.

tests.name: TestClaudeRetriesReceiveOnlyTheRemainingBudgetAndTurns
tests.says: Each Claude Code retry receives only remaining dollars and turns, including fractional dollar allowances without rounding upward.

tests.name: TestClaudeProviderRetriesCannotRenewAnExhaustedLimit
tests.says: A Claude Code run that exhausts its budget or turns stops without waiting or launching another attempt, retains usage and reports the exhausted limit.

tests.name: TestClaudeProviderRetryStopsAtTheRemainingLimit
tests.says: A Claude Code CLI honoring its supplied limits stops at the remaining budget or turn allowance instead of succeeding under renewed limits.

tests.name: TestCodexProviderRetriesShareTheStepLimit
tests.says: Codex attempts share one step allowance and stop before waiting or launching another attempt after exhausting it, retaining all attempts' usage.

tests.name: TestProviderRetriesShareMCPAllowance
tests.says: Both providers share one MCP call allowance across fresh servers during retries, including calls missing from gate logs and agent events; Codex explicitly forwards it in MCP configuration through a fixture that filters the server environment as Codex does, and a separate run gets its own allowance.

tests.name: TestClaudeIncompletePaidAttemptCannotRenewTheDollarBudget
tests.says: A Claude stream with paid assistant work followed by disconnect and no final cost reserves the remaining dollar budget as an incomplete conservative estimate, retains all observed turns and tools and the provider diagnostic, and launches no further attempt, including after an earlier paid failure.

tests.name: TestClaudeClosingResultsReconcilePaidAssistantUsage
tests.says: A closing Claude result supplies the authoritative cost and turns for its paid assistant work, so retry usage is summed once and the next attempt receives exactly the remaining dollar allowance.
